summary.name: Cyberpunk. Supplemental design reference, not a directly named style in the source collection. Digital and 3D Aesthetics category.
summary.visualIdentity: Explicitly: a technology-dense setting with legible social and industrial character, controlled neon, atmosphere, and localized reflections. The subject needs a clear luminance hierarchy. Devices, streets, or signal systems should visibly function, not rely only on purple-blue light, signs, or decorative HUDs.
summary.suitableUses: Explicitly: cyberpunk suits world-building scenes with a strong environment. A hybrid is advised when in-world interfaces or signal disruptions are story-critical. Suggested best fits are sci-fi story trailers, speculative product narratives, and hacking sequences. Other uses are unspecified.
summary.limitations: Explicitly: avoid a purple-blue wash everywhere and floating random HUD clutter. Glitch events must not be constant or strobing. Two-color contrast checks do not verify text over images, glass, video, or animated lighting. Simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production or validated physics.
summary.palette: Suggested, not supplied: background #111D25 (dominant layout role), foreground #F1F0E3, accent_1 #52B3AC, accent_2 #DAA259, accent_3 #B96887. Gradients are disabled. Task-supplied exact colors override these. Foreground on background measures 14.934. Background on accent_1 measures 6.852, on accent_2 7.578. Accent_3 fails the 4.5 text target and is decorative only. Recoloring or adding hues is not permitted.
summary.motionAndInteraction: The source defines no mandatory motion recipe for this style. Suggested optional motion patterns are motion-012 (chaptered handoff), motion-015 (narrative steps), and motion-020 (glitch cut), which explicitly lists Cyberpunk as a good fit. Video derives state from composition time. Interactive delivery may use scroll or keyboard input, with a reduced-motion cut or still background.
summary.audio: Unspecified by the style; no audio layer is mandated. The source offers options to consider: background music, voiceover, sung vocals, sound effects, ambience, or silence, chosen per topic and audience. No genre, tempo, or instrument is fixed. Explicit user audio requirements take priority. Speech intelligibility and clipping must be verified.
summary.assetRequirements: Unspecified in the source for images, models, and fonts. Suggested needs include local fonts and assets loaded before rendering, and PBR environment maps for metal, plastic, or glass. Interface text should be composited separately in SVG or HTML. Supplied artwork and exact colors must be preserved. Any missing assets must be stated rather than invented.
summary.combinations: Suggested hybrid style-112 provides diegetic interfaces that visibly operate within the scene, tied to in-world sources, with the subject brightest. Suggested style-067 provides brief signal-intrusion glitches only at transitions or story events, using primary accents. Both are inferred suggestions. Motion patterns motion-012, motion-015, and motion-020 are optional additions.
summary.productionApproach: Explicitly: Three.js with PBR materials and postprocessing (bloom, tone mapping) renders the scenes, and SVG or HTML handles text. GSAP drives a paused, seekable timeline for motion. HyperFrames is the primary pipeline for assembly, timing, sync, validation, and export. Remotion is a fallback only when HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation exists. Blender with bpy is listed as an alternative. Delivery requires inspecting key frames and watching the full video.
